1.title: Math Foundations
1.description: Basic arithmetic, simple algebra, and introductory geometry

chunks.content:
Arithmetic is the foundation of all mathematics. It deals with numbers and the basic operations: addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (×), and division (÷).

Key Rules:
• Addition: Combining quantities. 3 + 4 = 7
• Subtraction: Finding difference. 10 - 6 = 4
• Multiplication: Repeated addition. 3 × 4 = 12 (same as 4+4+4)
• Division: Splitting into equal groups. 12 ÷ 4 = 3

Order of Operations (BODMAS/PEMDAS):
Brackets → Orders (powers) → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction
Example: 2 + 3 × 4 = 2 + 12 = 14 (NOT 20)

Algebra uses letters (variables) to represent unknown numbers.

Core Concepts:
• Variable: A letter representing an unknown (x, y, z)
• Expression: Numbers and variables combined (2x + 3)
• Equation: An expression set equal to something (2x + 3 = 7)

Solving Simple Equations:
To solve 2x = 8, divide both sides by 2:
2x ÷ 2 = 8 ÷ 2
x = 4

Always do the SAME operation to BOTH sides.

Practice: Solve 3x + 2 = 11
Step 1: 3x = 11 - 2 = 9
Step 2: x = 9 ÷ 3 = 3

Geometry studies shapes, sizes, and properties of figures.

Basic Shapes:
• Rectangle: Area = length × width, Perimeter = 2(l + w)
• Triangle: Area = ½ × base × height
• Circle: Area = πr², Circumference = 2πr (π ≈ 3.14159)

Angles:
• Acute: Less than 90°
• Right: Exactly 90°
• Obtuse: Between 90° and 180°
• Straight: Exactly 180°

The angles of any triangle always add up to 180°.

2.title: Intermediate Mathematics
2.description: Quadratic equations, trigonometry, and statistical analysis

chunks.content:
A quadratic equation has the form ax² + bx + c = 0.

Methods to Solve:
1. Factoring: Find two numbers that multiply to ac and add to b
   Example: x² + 5x + 6 = 0 → (x+2)(x+3) = 0 → x = -2 or x = -3

2. Quadratic Formula: x = (-b ± √(b²-4ac)) / 2a
   The discriminant (b²-4ac) tells you:
   • Positive: Two real solutions
   • Zero: One real solution
   • Negative: No real solutions

3. Completing the Square:
   x² + 6x + 5 = 0
   (x + 3)² - 9 + 5 = 0
   (x + 3)² = 4
   x + 3 = ±2 → x = -1 or x = -5

A function maps each input to exactly one output: f(x) = expression.

Types of Functions:
• Linear: f(x) = mx + b (straight line, m = slope, b = y-intercept)
• Quadratic: f(x) = ax² + bx + c (parabola)
• Exponential: f(x) = aˣ (rapid growth/decay)

Key Graph Concepts:
• Domain: All valid input values (x values)
• Range: All possible output values (y values)
• Intercepts: Where the graph crosses the axes
• Slope = rise/run = (y₂-y₁)/(x₂-x₁)

Transformations:
• f(x) + k shifts UP by k
• f(x) - k shifts DOWN by k
• f(x + h) shifts LEFT by h

Statistics analyzes data; probability predicts outcomes.

Measures of Central Tendency:
• Mean: Sum of all values ÷ count
• Median: Middle value when sorted
• Mode: Most frequent value

Measures of Spread:
• Range: Max - Min
• Variance: Average of squared deviations from mean
• Standard Deviation (σ): Square root of variance — measures how spread out data is

Probability Basics:
• P(event) = favorable outcomes / total outcomes
• P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) [if independent]
• P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)

3.title: Advanced Mathematics
3.description: Calculus, linear algebra, and complex problem-solving

chunks.content:
Calculus studies continuous change. The derivative measures the rate of change.

Derivative Rules:
• Power Rule: d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹
  Example: d/dx(x⁴) = 4x³
• Sum Rule: d/dx(f + g) = f' + g'
• Product Rule: d/dx(fg) = f'g + fg'
• Chain Rule: d/dx(f(g(x))) = f'(g(x)) · g'(x)

Common Derivatives:
• d/dx(sin x) = cos x
• d/dx(cos x) = -sin x
• d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ
• d/dx(ln x) = 1/x

Applications: Finding maxima/minima by setting f'(x) = 0 (critical points).

Integration is the reverse of differentiation — it finds accumulated quantities.

Basic Integration Rules:
• ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C (n ≠ -1)
• ∫eˣ dx = eˣ + C
• ∫sin x dx = -cos x + C
• ∫cos x dx = sin x + C

Definite Integrals:
∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a) where F is the antiderivative.
This represents the AREA under the curve f(x) from a to b.

Fundamental Theorem of Calculus:
If F'(x) = f(x), then ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a)

Techniques: Substitution, Integration by Parts (∫u dv = uv - ∫v du)

Limits describe the behavior of a function as x approaches a value.

Notation: lim(x→a) f(x) = L means f(x) approaches L as x approaches a.

Key Limits:
• lim(x→0) sin(x)/x = 1
• lim(x→∞) (1 + 1/x)ˣ = e
• lim(x→0) (eˣ - 1)/x = 1

L'Hôpital's Rule:
If limit gives 0/0 or ∞/∞, then:
lim(x→a) f(x)/g(x) = lim(x→a) f'(x)/g'(x)

Continuity: A function is continuous at x = a if:
1. f(a) is defined
2. lim(x→a) f(x) exists
3. lim(x→a) f(x) = f(a)
